tool_args.rationale: The previous static attempt was refuted, while the follow-up batch supplies nine rows spanning input and sink gradient. Fit the two documented open branch forms numerically (signed square-root source versus linear leak) and select the lower-residual branch. The fixed horizon does not justify a temporal model, and gradients remain below the avalanche regime.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The existing nine observations include the prior open-branch point and broad input/gradient variation, so the candidate branches can be compared by numerical fit without another measurement.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit a coupled memory ODE or dual-horizon law
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: All rows have the same short horizon and fixed initial state; those temporal parameters are not identifiable here, while the expanded evidence specifically supports the siphon family.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the avalanche siphon or high-gradient probe
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Observed sink gradients top out at 2.2, below the noted threshold region; the avalanche term is not activated by these training observations.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit Haldane, Cobb-Douglas, or a nuisance auxiliary
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The evidence supports an input-saturating sink-gradient siphon with an open additive branch; these alternatives do not use the documented mechanism evidence, and nuisance measurements are explicitly irrelevant.
